correctness.rationale: The explicitly defined eleven-vertex, eighteen-edge graph has 222 Hamiltonian spanning-path facets, independently confirmed by DFS and a Held-Karp recurrence. Their downward closure has 37,454 nonempty faces. The exact listed vertex-toggle matching has 18,724 pairs and only one critical 0-cell and five critical 6-cells. Complete Kahn topological sort of all 237,072 directed codimension-one incidences proves global acyclicity, so discrete Morse theory gives five six-spheres integrally. The graph automorphism group is all six permutations of the three intrinsic degree-four vertices times the involution exchanging the two intrinsic degree-three hubs; every induced edge permutation is enumerated. Exact signed fixed-simplex traces of all twelve group elements give the character (5,-1,-1,1,-1,1), whose irreducible decomposition is (sgn+Std)⊗trivial+(Std)⊗sign. All computations were replayed directly with the included checker under two Python hash seeds.

originality.rationale: Comparisons by face definition and implication (not title alone) distinguish the spanning-path down-closure of the Herschel edge set from the fixed-vertex non-Hamiltonian graph property, vertex independence complexes, generic path ideals, and previous graph-specific spanning-path results. A semantic mathematical-record search, open-literature searches under aliases, and primary/source previews found no theorem assigning these exact Herschel homotopy and rational symmetry invariants. Older relevant full text could not all be read; this is a best-knowledge novelty assessment, not proof of priority.

value.rationale: A natural, canonical object is involved: the smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph, which nevertheless admits spanning paths. The full downward-closed complex measures which partial edge choices extend to a spanning path, a finer property than traceability or the path count. Its pure dimension is nine but its complete integral homotopy lies in dimension six with rank five, requiring a nontrivial acyclic matching on 37,454 faces. The full natural twelve-element graph symmetry acts nontrivially on the entire top homology and has no fixed class, a structural invariant not determined by the graph count or existing independence-complex results. It yields a reusable exact benchmark for path-extendibility topology, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
